sections.h2: What sort of place is Jeff Davis County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Farming and timber define Jeff Davis County, down in Georgia's southeast. The seat is Hazlehurst, the largest community; Denton is the lone other city; and lawmakers established the county on August 18, 1905, per Wikipedia.

The area is 335 square miles, 331 of it land. Cotton and peanuts lead the crops, tobacco once counted for more, and timber stays a steady product. Wheeler, Montgomery, Toombs, Appling, Bacon, Coffee and Telfair counties touch its borders. Water leaves in several directions: toward the Lower Ocmulgee along the north and part of the west, into the Altamaha in the east, and to the Little Satilla and Satilla in the south.

Satilla is a census-designated place, while Roper, Snipesville and Tallahassee are unincorporated crossroads. A house in Hazlehurst, a country place near a crossroads and a cut-over timber tract each attract different buyers.

sections.h2: How affordable is housing in Jeff Davis County?
sections.html:
Very. For 2020-2024, QuickFacts gives $118,300 as the middle value of an owned home, and owners occupy 71.3% of homes.

The count climbed to 15,068 in 2010, dipped to 14,779 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate sits 3.0% above the 2020 number. Renters occupied 33.1% of homes in 2020, and rentals stood 9.4% vacant. With only nine permits in 2025, new construction barely competes with resales, so a seller mostly faces other older houses.

sections.h2: Who lives in Jeff Davis County, and why should a seller care?
sections.html:
Households are numerous and settled. QuickFacts lists 5,484 of them at 2.70 people apiece, and 89.3% of residents had not moved in the past year, so many buyers already know the neighborhood.

Children are 24.4% of residents and seniors 17.0%. A bachelor's degree is held by 13.2% of adults, and 77.3% completed high school. Households with broadband total 76.6%, a detail worth stating in a rural listing. In 2023 the county had 260 employer establishments and 3,834 jobs, and 2022 retail sales reached $201,004,000.

Those numbers describe a buyer pool that leans local, which is why paid tax receipts and a clear title help in a market this size.

sections.h2: Where do Jeff Davis County taxpayers go with questions?
sections.html:
Begin at the Tax Commissioner, 14 Jeff Davis Street, Suite 104, Hazlehurst, GA 31539, telephone (912) 375-6622. Letters go to PO Box 558, and weekday service ends at 4:30.

  • Tax Commissioner: sends and collects bills, hands out mobile home decals, and also takes timber, heavy duty equipment and intangible tax
  • Tax Assessor, (912) 375-6624: sets values and receives appeals
  • Board of Equalization: the Grand Jury names its members to rule on value disputes
  • Commission and school board: choose the millage rates

An online payment portal also exists. Check with the office on the best method before you mail a check near a deadline.

sections.h2: How fast do penalties grow on a late Jeff Davis County bill?
sections.html:
They stack up. The normal mailing date is October 20 and the due date December 20; part payments are fine until then, and afterward interest builds monthly at the bank prime rate.

Every 120 days brings another 5% penalty, ending at 20%. A balance left for a year grows noticeably, and any payoff quote goes stale fast.

  • Mobile homes: January mailing, April 1 due date, and a decal displayed after payment
  • Past April 1: a 10% filing penalty plus 1% monthly, then a FiFa on the clerk's docket and possible auction
  • A mobile home on land the owner holds can be homesteaded and is then taxed like real property

Another county page lists May 1 for mobile homes, so check with the office before relying on either.

sections.h2: What does the Jeff Davis County homestead exemption cover?
sections.html:
The base exemption deducts two thousand dollars from assessed value. It applies to county and school taxes but leaves out municipal school levies and bond debt.

File at the Tax Commissioner's counter from January 1 to April 1, between 8 and 5 on weekdays. The county says state law grants no extension, so a missed date gives up the exemption for that year. Once approved it renews until your circumstances change, and it never exceeds the tax owed.

  • Conservation use and residential transitional property
  • Agricultural preferential assessment
  • Rehabilitated historic property

Each of those three programs asks the owner to covenant with the Tax Assessor to maintain qualifying use for ten years or more. If you plan to sell enrolled land, phone (912) 375-6624 and ask what the covenant demands of a new owner.

sections.h2: What can I do if I think my Jeff Davis County value is too high?
sections.html:
Write to the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice and name the appeal method you prefer. Spring is when notices for real and personal property usually go out.

The county accepts four grounds: whether the property is taxable, its value, its uniformity with similar parcels, or a denied exemption. Objecting to the rate or the bill's size does not qualify. A return filed between January 1 and April 1 can state your own January 1 opinion of market value and protects your appeal rights if the figure changes. Mobile home owners have 45 days from the bill mailing, then 21 days after a change notice to go before the Board of Equalization.

sections.h2: How should I prepare to sell a Jeff Davis County property with tax outstanding?
sections.html:
Obtain a written payoff from the Tax Commissioner and have the closing office settle it out of your proceeds. Interest runs every month and penalties step up each 120 days, so an old quote may fall short.

Timber land may owe timber tax, billed by the same office. If your mobile home sits on rented ground, confirm the decal and the April 1 bill before listing. A FiFa on the clerk's docket is public record, so a title search will turn it up.

sections.h2: What do returns and spring notices involve in Jeff Davis County?
sections.html:
Owners return taxable property to the Tax Assessors Office from January 1 through April 1. When nothing is filed, last year's value and last year's real property exemptions carry over.

Appraisers use recent sales and market conditions as of January 1, and the spring notice states each parcel's value. A return of your own with a January 1 opinion keeps your appeal right alive if the figure is revised.

  • Tell the county about a new mailing address quickly, since notices follow the last one on file
  • Approved exemptions renew yearly until eligibility changes

faqs.q: What is the payment date for Jeff Davis County property tax?
faqs.a: December 20. The usual mailing date is October 20, and partial payments are accepted up to the deadline.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Jeff Davis County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: Dial (912) 375-6622 or visit 14 Jeff Davis Street, Suite 104, in Hazlehurst. For valuation, phone the Tax Assessor at (912) 375-6624.

faqs.q: What does lateness cost on a Jeff Davis County bill?
faqs.a: Monthly interest at the bank prime rate, plus 5% every 120 days up to a 20% cap. A mobile home paid after April 1 owes 10% plus 1% a month.

faqs.q: When can Jeff Davis County owners claim homestead?
faqs.a: From January 1 through April 1 for that tax year; the county says Georgia law offers no extension.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline in Jeff Davis County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date. Put the appeal in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors and state your method.
